extracted.intended_audience: creative writers, literature students, and readers studying narrative structure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on composing and understanding the denouement — the element of story structure in which plot lines come to resolution and events are explained, normally following the climax. Useful for writers deciding how to end a narrative and for students analysing narrative closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot lines come to a resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: All plot lines typically come to a resolution; events are explained, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core function of a denouement: to resolve outstanding threads and explain events. It usually follows the climax and may be followed by a conclusion or epilogue which can give a moral or outline subsequent events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement relative to the climax
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most narratives place the denouement after the climax; some taxonomies additionally separate a 'falling action' between the climax and the denouement. Note that some authors (or forms) may treat placement differently—e.g., Henry Albert Philips includes the denouement in the 'conclusion'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with falling action
rubrics_metrics.description: It is common to include the 'falling action' between the climax and the denouement (see 'List of story structures').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When structuring an ending, consider whether falling action is needed to bridge the climax and the denouement or whether the denouement itself will carry the resolution. Shorter forms may omit extended falling action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate length and economy for short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories, with their economy of words, often do not need an elaborate denouement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the denouement's depth and length to the form: allow more succinct or implied resolution in short fiction to preserve pacing and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can function as a teaser (non-end placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically a denouement is at the end of the narrative, but it may also start the story, acting as a teaser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reversing expectations by opening with a denouement-like scene to hook readers; ensure subsequent narrative justifies the choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation: logical follow-through versus deus ex machina
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually a denouement follows the logic of the course of the events, but sometimes it may be unmotivated, what is called 'deus ex machina'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer resolutions that follow from prior events and character/action logic. Avoid unmotivated solutions (deus ex machina) unless employing that device intentionally and with awareness of its effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Happy ending as a common denouement type
rubrics_metrics.description: Another common type of a denouement is a happy ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A denouement can close with a 'happy ending' or other tonal resolutions; an epilogue or conclusion may explicitly state future happiness or moral ('lived happily ever after'). Choose tone to suit genre and thematic aims.
